# Pinned .NET GUID parsing observations

`guid_parse.dotnet.json` is the **unchanged actual framework capture**, not
expectations generated by the Go parser or by source predictions. It supports
one explicit opt-in `concepts.ParseDotNetGUID` compatibility-conversion API.
Existing strict UUID codecs and the eleven `scalars.json` fixtures are unchanged.

## Schema version 1

All section IDs are unique: **945**, not 945 equivalent Go inputs.

| Section | Rows | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `cases` | 923 | Valid-UTF-8 string inputs: 641 Parse successes, 282 failures; built-in Guid JSON has 16 successes and 907 failures |
| `dotNetDiagnostics` | 6 | Null string and unpaired UTF-16 code units; no equivalent Go inputs asserted |
| `rawJsonControls` | 12 | Four successes, eight failures; separate JSON syntax/conversion boundary |
| `goInvalidUtf8Seeds` | 4 | Invalid byte strings rejected by Go; never executed by .NET, no .NET outcomes |

`cases` contains ordered `id`, `input`, exact `inputUtf8Hex`, `prediction`,
`parse`, `tryParse` and `builtInJson`. Predictions are annotations, never the
source of test expectations. Result `accepted` is an explicit JSON boolean.
Successful `canonicalD` and `rfcBytesHex` are lowercase dashed text and sixteen
RFC/network-order bytes from `ToByteArray(bigEndian: true)`. Failed Parse has
explicit null value fields and a recorded exception type. Failed TryParse
records Guid.Empty. Parse and TryParse agree for every case and diagnostic.
Go tests do not match CLR exception names or messages.

`builtInJson` records serialized input and an independent built-in Guid JSON
result. Successful string JSON values agree with Parse. Raw JSON controls store
raw syntax, exact UTF-8 bytes and results separately. Diagnostics retain exact
UTF-16 units; the validator checks unpaired units and the serializer's replacement
representation rather than inventing valid Go strings. Invalid-UTF8 seeds have
only ID, bytes and disposition.

Metadata requires the complete environment, assembly identities, runtime/source
pins, exact four source filenames/hashes, plan digest and input digest. The latter
hashes compact UTF-8 System.Text.Json serialization of ordered `{id,input}` rows.
The portable validator recomputes it from emitted string lexemes, avoiding a
Python approximation of System.Text.Json escaping. It rejects duplicate members,
missing/null acceptance, noninteger counts and incomplete metadata. Immutable
capture bytes and full-row comparison lock boundary IDs to their exact inputs.

Coverage: 20 canonical, 60 individual hex-case mutations, 375 surrounding-whitespace,
75 non-whitespace, 333 X numeric/internal-whitespace, 12 D compatibility and
48 malformed/wrapper/URN/punctuation cases. The exact 25 whitespace characters
are listed in the capture; they are not Go's generic whitespace predicate.

X preserves legacy empty-after-prefix zero values, deliberate uint16 truncation
in fields two/three, byte guards and leading-zero lengths. D preserves fixed
boundaries, triggered fallback and its final 4+8 split/conditional NUL behavior.
This corpus is evidence, not an exhaustive test of all possible strings or
future runtimes. Compatibility conversion is not canonical-input validation or
correlation admission. Callers must limit untrusted payload sizes.

## Optional framework-only reproduction

Ordinary Go CI reads the committed capture and does not need .NET. The optional
[portable harness](https://github.com/Cratis/Fundamentals.Go/tree/develop/ContractTests/GuidParsing)
requires SDK 10.0.401 and runtime 10.0.12. From the repository root:

```sh
mkdir -p .ai-work/guid-reproduction
cd ContractTests/GuidParsing
dotnet build GuidParseProbe.csproj -c Release --configfile NuGet.Config \
  -p:ImportDirectoryBuildProps=false -p:ImportDirectoryBuildTargets=false
dotnet bin/Release/net10.0/GuidParseProbe.dll \
  ../../.ai-work/guid-reproduction/capture.new.json
python3 -B compare.py ../../.ai-work/guid-reproduction/capture.new.json
```

Use a **new** output path; the writer refuses replacement. `python3 -B compare.py`
alone validates the frozen capture without .NET. Run validator regression tests
with `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s ContractTests/GuidParsing -p 'test_*.py'`
from the repository root.

The public harness intentionally declares **`portable-guid-parse-v1`**, not the
historical source profile. Only `Program.cs` changed: the ignored-plan file read
was replaced with the historical digest and explicit portable-profile/original-
capture metadata. Its new source hash is recorded in each new capture; original
metadata is never rewritten to pretend the sources were identical. The three
config-file hashes must remain historical. The comparator checks current public
source hashes and package-free assets/runtime configuration, requires all other
metadata invariants, permits OS/architecture and runtime-file line-ending
variation, and compares all observation/diagnostic/seed rows exactly. Capture
profile and source identity changes are distinct from behavioral equivalence.

No compiled outputs, restored assets or personal caches are distributed.
Framework APIs/source links are Microsoft .NET (MIT); synthetic harness and
observations are distributed under this repository's MIT license.
